design_soundness.reasoning: The report gives explicit, checkable subtyping rules (TABLE/ROW, SCH-CLOSED, SCH-OPEN-L/R, NAME-IN/NAME-IN-X/NAME-NEW/NAME-STR, COL-SAME/COL-OTHER) and the diff's constrainSchema/constrainColumnMembership functions implement exactly this decomposition, so the argument is grounded in code rather than assertion. Restrictions are independently justified rather than hand-waved: sort covariance is tied to cell immutability, name/order invariance is tied to distinct-name and append-only schema evolution, and the rejection of record-type schemas is argued concretely (record subtyping is width-permissive and would mis-describe column-names()/stack). Wherever a schema prefix or column name is unresolved, the design defers the constraint to the enclosing level and ultimately degrades to Any/opaque Table rather than guessing (documented in code and in DESIGN.md §5), which is the right conservative behavior for a sound system. Score is not a full 1.0 because the argument is presented, not machine-verified (no metatheory or exhaustive proof), and a few solver branches (e.g. t-column vs t-column 'different schemas' using only the name, not the recorded sort, to look up the target) would need closer scrutiny to fully rule out edge-case gaps.

examples_quality.reasoning: The ten example files are substantial and varied: direct B2T2 ports (dot-product, table-api, group-by, p-hacking, quiz-scores, example-tables), core.arr ports (summary-stats, table-helpers), full syntax-form coverage (table-syntax-forms), and an external-data scenario (load-table-annotations). They genuinely exercise schema-dependent typing — column reads recovering exact List<T>, build/add-column producing widened schema types, select/extract computing exact projected schemas, and group-by propagating a key column's own name/sort into the result type — rather than being trivial programs that merely happen to type-check.
